Thought: I need to determine what products are generated when thiocarbamates and dithiocarbamates thermally decompose. Let me think about the chemistry involved.

Thiocarbamates have the general structure R-O-C(=S)-NR2, while dithiocarbamates have the structure R-S-C(=S)-NR2. When these compounds undergo thermal decomposition, they break down into simpler molecules.

From my knowledge of organic chemistry, when these sulfur-containing compounds decompose thermally, they typically produce carbon disulfide (CS2) and other sulfur-containing products like hydrogen sulfide (H2S). This is because the C=S bonds in these compounds break during thermal decomposition.

Looking at the options, B (Carbon disulfide and hydrogen sulfide) seems most consistent with the thermal decomposition of these sulfur-containing compounds.
Final Answer: The thermal decomposition of thiocarbamates and dithiocarbamates typically produces carbon disulfide (CS2) and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) as the main products.
